document_understanding.design_overview: This Figma design represents the UI/UX for an Ecommerce Cart workflow. It covers the user journey from product selection, cart review, quantity adjustments, to checkout initiation. The design emphasizes clarity, ease of navigation, and efficient cart management.
user_flows: User browses Product Listing > selects a product > views Product Detail > adds product to Cart > views Cart Overview > proceeds to Checkout.
User adjusts item quantity in Cart Overview > updates reflected in real-time.
User removes item from Cart > confirmation dialog appears > item removed on confirmation.
User proceeds from Cart Overview to Checkout > reviews Order Summary > confirms purchase.
component_usage: Product Card: Displays product image, name, price, and add-to-cart button.
Add to Cart Button: Prominent action button on product cards and detail screens.
Cart Icon with Badge: Persistent navigation element showing cart item count.
Quantity Stepper: Allows increment/decrement of item quantity in cart.
Remove Item Button: Triggers confirmation dialog for item removal.
Checkout Button: Primary action in cart overview, styled for emphasis.
Order Summary Card: Summarizes items, subtotal, taxes, and total.
Empty State Illustration: Visual cue for empty cart, with call-to-action.
design_assumptions: Users expect real-time feedback when adjusting item quantities.
Cart contents persist across navigation within the session.
Checkout flow is linear and requires all cart items to be validated before proceeding.
Empty cart state encourages users to return to product listing.
design_gaps: No explicit error handling UI for failed add-to-cart actions.
Missing validation for maximum allowed quantity per item.
No indication of stock availability on cart overview.
No guest checkout option visible in the checkout flow.
document_understanding.final_conclusion: The Ecommerce Cart Figma design provides a clear, user-friendly workflow for cart management and checkout. While the core flows and components are well-represented, enhancements around error handling, validation, and guest checkout could further improve the user experience.
